binaryNote: graph_probe.baseline ... graph_probe.item8b are copies of target/debug/examples/graph_probe taken after each build; graph_probe.final is build 13 (Servo at servoHead). Builds 0 to 7c enable WebGL2 for every origin (the example sets dom_webgl2_enabled after Engine::start, the recipe of the first run) and load the pages from http://127.0.0.1:8765; item8, item8b and final take --notes-root and load frame-notes://probe/... with WebGL2 on for the frame-notes scheme only. control-* runs are earlier binaries run again at the load of the final runs.

libraries.v3: @cosmos.gl/graph 3.5.1 with @luma.gl/core, engine, webgl and shadertools 9.3.6 (WebGL2), loaded from esm.sh

items.what: WebGL2 extensions the native GL supports
items.result: getSupportedExtensions() lists 6 extensions instead of none
luma.gl's copyTexSubImage3D call no longer throws
[0, 0] became [1, 64]; core profiles have POINT_SIZE_RANGE, not ALIASED_POINT_SIZE_RANGE

items.what: drawBuffers and readBuffer on the default framebuffer
items.result: DrawBuffers GL errors went from 468 in item3-v3 to 0 in item4-v3
RGBA32F, RGBA32I, RGBA32UI and the other pairs of ES 3.0 4.3.2 read back; texImage2D keeps the sized internal format that the read-back type depends on
12 failed DetachShader calls in the delete/replace cycle of program-lifecycle.html went to 0 (item6-lifecycle-before and item6-lifecycle-after)

four separate causes: texStorage2D rejected non power of two sizes so the position and force textures were never allocated; uniform block names kept ANGLE's _u prefix so luma.gl dropped every draw call; texSubImage2D refused RG, RED and *_INTEGER formats; and Apple GL's fast math folded isnan() so every point kept its NaN size and color

items.frame: src/engine.rs sets dom_webgl2_enabled_schemes to frame-notes and registers the scheme handler passed to Engine::start_with_protocols
items.result: scheme-gate: WebGL2 context and all six WebGL2 interfaces on frame-notes:, none on http:

items.what: framebufferTextureLayer and the WebGL2 unpack parameters, found by running the conformance suite
items.result: 3D texture readback correct; UNPACK_ROW_LENGTH, UNPACK_IMAGE_HEIGHT and the skip parameters honored (unpack-params.html)

items.what: regressions the conformance suite found in the commits above
items.result: no conformance file passes fewer subtests than before, apart from the files listed under wpt.fileLevel

servoshellBuilds.command: ./mach build --dev (through the space-free symlink, see wpt.runner)

control.note: Chromium in the Claude desktop app's built-in browser, run on 2026-10-25

canvasControl.note: force-graph 1.52.0 on Canvas 2D; Frame measured 13 fps on 2026-10-25 and 17 fps here, both debug builds

fpsNote: fps is the number of requestAnimationFrame callbacks in 5 s, in a debug build, on a machine that other builds shared. The same binary (item7c, item8b) gave 7 to 11 fps at a load average of 50 to 70 and 83 to 84 fps at a load average of 18 to 25 (control-* runs), so compare fps only between runs with a similar loadAverage1m. Chromium: 120 fps, with the simulation on.

wpt.runner: ./mach test-wpt --binary <servoshell> --pref dom_webgl2_enabled=true --processes 6, over tests/wpt/webgl/tests/conformance2 and the 17 conformance directories the changes touch. mach refuses a checkout whose path has a space, so it ran through a symlink without one (the working directory stayed the real repository root for resources/wpt-prefs.json, PYTHONPATH=<symlink>/tests/wpt/tests, absolute symlink test paths). The .ini expectation files were recorded with WebGL2 off and were not rewritten, so pass counts are counted from the raw log, not from the expectations.
wpt.subtestNote: WebGL conformance subtests are named by assertion index, so only the pass counts per file are compared; the per-name comparison reports 151 'regressions' that are assertions whose index moved.

fileLevel.basePass: 54, 62, 54, 90 of 54, 62, 54, 94 (three single-process runs, then the full suite)
fileLevel.verdict: not a regression: the number of subtests this file reports varies from run to run on the base build too

fileLevel.full suite: CRASH on the second build, OK on the base build
fileLevel.rerun: OK with 77 of 77, 11 of 11 and 4 of 6 on both builds, in two single-process reruns each
fileLevel.verdict: not a regression: the 6-process full suite crashes different files on each run (ext-blend-minmax crashes on the base build and passes on the second)

gaps: RGB10_A2 readPixels with UNSIGNED_INT_2_10_10_10_REV is not accepted
SRGB8_ALPHA8 readback needs GL_FRAMEBUFFER_SRGB on desktop GL (read-pixels-from-fbo-test #111 and #113)
multisampled depth and stencil renderbuffer validation
no clear* buffer type match validation (clear-func-buffer-type-match)
RED_BITS, DEPTH_BITS and the like on a framebuffer object (framebuffer-object-attachment)
WebGL1 createVertexArray fails with 0x502 on the macOS 2.1 compatibility context
validate_framebuffer and get_current_framebuffer_size still use the draw framebuffer, so a read framebuffer of another size is mis-measured
extensions not implemented: WEBGL_debug_renderer_info, EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2, EXT_texture_norm16, WEBGL_provoking_vertex, EXT_depth_clamp
WebGL2 overloads still commented out: texImage3D PBO and TexImageSource, other texSubImage3D forms, texSubImage2D PBO and srcOffset, compressedTex*3D
x != x on a NaN stays false in shaders on Apple GL (fast math); isnan() is repaired, comparisons cannot be
existing TexImage2D bug compares an element count with a byte offset; not changed

unitTests.pixelunpack: 6 passed (rustc --test on pixelunpack.rs, which uses only std; the servo-script test target was not built)
unitTests.shaderisnan: 4 passed (rustc --test on shaderisnan.rs, which uses only std)

limitations: passed on a graph-probe run means cosmos.gl initialised without throwing; nodePixels is the check that nodes were drawn

nodePixels counts pixels of the node color #e8973a in a screenshot taken 1.5 s after load; with the simulation on, the layout is mid-motion and the count differs from run to run (24 to 52 thousand), with the simulation off it is stable (about 109 thousand)
the errors 'uncaught exception: undefined @ :0:1' and 'ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications' appear in every run, including the baseline, and do not come from WebGL
the Chromium controls were not re-run on 2026-10-26; they are the 2026-10-25 files
